values.note: Single non-electric site $20, the one electric site $30; $10 a night per additional vehicle; group loop (Sapinero) $175 a night for 1-50 people, $275 for 51-100. Same on recreation.gov for 2026-2028.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/gmug/recreation/silver-jack-campground-ouray-rd ('Single Site Non-Electric: $20 per night | Single Site Electric: $30 per night | Additional Vehicle Fee: $10 per night. | Group Site: $175 per night (1-50 people), $275 per night (51-100 people)') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10130478/rates (2026: StandardNonelectric 20, StandardElectric 30), read 2026-10-28

values.note: 60 sites in three loops: Chipeta (25 sites) and Ouray (19, incl. electric site 7) for individual campers; Sapinero is a 16-site group loop. No agency page states a vehicle length; the catalog has none.

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/gmug/recreation/silver-jack-campground-ouray-rd ('Silver Jack Campground has 60 campsites around three loops - Chipeta, Ouray and Sapinero'; 'One of the three loops is often used for groups') + recreation.gov catalog for 10130478 (Chipeta Loop 25, Ouray Loop 19, 'Sapinero Loop' GroupLoop-16Sites; no Max Vehicle Length attribute), read 2026-10-28; the stored 45 ft came from note prose with no agency source

values.note: No cell signal and no nearby town for supplies. Bear country.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/gmug/recreation/silver-jack-campground-ouray-rd ('Vault toilet(s)'; 'Yes, drinking water is available'; 'There are no close communities to get provisions') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10130478 (notice 'NO cell signal is available'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Early summer to early fall, weather dependent (FS). recreation.gov's 2026 fee seasons run June 1 - September 30.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/gmug/recreation/silver-jack-campground-ouray-rd ('Seasons of Use: Early Summer to Early Fall - weather dependent'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: All 44 individual sites (Chipeta and Ouray loops) are 'Not Reservable' on recreation.gov, so first come, first served; only the 16-site Sapinero group loop books on recreation.gov. The FS page says 'This site has a combination of first come, first serve and reservable campsites.'

booking.source: recreation.gov campsite catalog for 10130478 (43 STANDARD NONELECTRIC and 1 STANDARD ELECTRIC sites campsite_status 'Not Reservable'; 'GROUP STANDARD NONELECTRIC' Sapinero Loop 'Open', reservable) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/gmug/recreation/silver-jack-campground-ouray-rd (sentence quoted), read 2026-10-28

note: Uncompahgre NF (Ouray RD) campground ~18 mi up Cimarron Rd (CR 858) from US-50, ~8,900 ft, just north of (below) the Silver Jack Reservoir dam; three loops heavily wooded with aspen and a few spruce over tall grass and wildflowers. Trails around the Cimarron Ridge and OHV trails nearby. --Claude
summary: FS page + recreation.gov + catalog: confirmed 60 sites, $20 non-electric, vault toilets, drinking water. Changed booking reservable/some_sites -> first-come always (all 44 individual sites Not Reservable; only the group loop books), fees 20/30 -> $20 base + $10 electric surcharge, cleared note-derived max_rig_ft 45 (no agency length). Added season note, fees checked 2026. Note rewritten: field facts dropped.
flags: Booking conflict: the FS page says 'This site has a combination of first come, first serve and reservable campsites. Please visit recreation.gov to secure your reservation.' The recreation.gov catalog marks all 43 standard and the 1 electric individual site 'Not Reservable' (reservable sites at other CO campgrounds read 'Open' in the same off-season catalog); only the Sapinero group loop is reservable. Recorded first-come for individual sites.

Length: no agency figure. The stored 45 ft ('vehicles up to 45 ft') came from note prose; neither the FS page nor recreation.gov states a length, and the catalog has no Max Vehicle Length. Cleared. Nothing singles the campground out for small rigs.

Phone missing: Ouray Ranger District (970) 240-5300 (GMUG conditions page and the Gold Mountain closure order contact). recreation.gov's facility phone 928-537-8888 (camping@rrmofa.com) is the concessionaire, Recreation Resource Management, Lakeside AZ.
Operator: concessionaire (Recreation Resource Management, per recreation.gov's contact details) on Uncompahgre NF land; ownership left federal.

Gold Mountain Fire: closure order #02-04-06-26-29 (v4.0, effective September 15, 2026 to May 31, 2027) closes Middle Fork Cimarron Road NFSR 861.1, Cow Creek Road NFSR 857, Dexter Creek NFSR 871, Cutler NFSR 872, Jackass Flats NFSR 871.2 and Blowout NFSR 871.2B plus trails; it does NOT name CR 858 (Cimarron Rd) or Silver Jack Campground. The FS page shows a 'Site Closed' badge (last updated September 17, 2026), consistent with its season ending (recreation.gov's 2026 fees run to September 30); no closure notice is given.

Road: no agency wording on CR 858's condition beyond the directions ('travel approximately 18 miles south, past Big Cimarron and Beaver Lake Campgrounds'); GMUG's conditions page says to call the Ouray RD at 970-240-5300 for road conditions.

Pin 38.23811,-107.53511 (the FS point) is at the campground entrance on CR 858; the loops are west of the road, centred ~38.2370,-107.5386 (~330 m W). recreation.gov's facility point 38.23611,-107.53762 is inside the middle loop. Within tolerance, but the recreation.gov point is the better pin; the catalog has no site coordinates.

Waterfront (stored not waterfront, confirmed): on Esri imagery Silver Jack Reservoir lies SOUTH of its dam, and the loops are north of the dam (downstream), the nearest loop ~200 m from the water behind the dam embankment. Below the dam is not on the lake.
